This is also reproducible in 3.1, 3.6, and 4.0.4, so it is not a recent regression.

I dug into this a bit, and the main problems that keep this from being easily fixed are: 
1. Classes require a file path when being registered (which dynamic scripts do not have)
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/dc5f1b7a2826962f02230227abc486ac160ae66c/core/object/script_language.cpp#L395
2. Classes are currently only registered by the editor and saved at export (this explains why saving it and using `load()` did not work)
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/dc5f1b7a2826962f02230227abc486ac160ae66c/editor/editor_file_system.cpp#L2425

One option to fix this would be removing the `path` from GlobalScriptClass and replace it with `source_code`, but that would involve a major refactoring, possibly reduce performance, and likely break compatibility. Another option would be to generate temporary files for dynamic scripts and register the class upon `reload()`. I'm not sure if an API for creating temporary files in `res://` exists. Another approach could be to create a second type of global classes, for example `struct DynamicGlobalScriptClass`, that has dynamic loading functionality without the need for a path, including only enough functionality to fix this bug and related issues. All of these approaches, unfortunately, would add substantial complexity. Regardless of the approach, `ScriptServer::add_global_class(...)` probably needs to be called somewhere inside `GDScript::reload()`, or a related or sub-function, when processing a new `class_name`.

I'm not familiar enough with the codebase as a whole to comment on which approach (if any) would be the best, so I'll leave this here in the hope it will be useful to a more knowledgeable contributor.

Thank you @0xcafeb33f for tracking this down. I found a possible workaround. Loading a resource pack refreshes the script name cache, so loading a resource pack should do the trick. However, so far it seems I am failing to produce a valid resource pack dynamically. (This code is written for Godot Unit Test.)

```gdscript
var id := 1
var mod_file := test_data_dir + "test_%d.zip"%[id]
var file_name := "empty_test_object_%d.gd"%[id]
# This creates the contents of the file:
var schema_text := schema.generate_gdscript()
var gdscript_class_name := "EmptyTestObject%d"%[id]

var packer := ZIPPacker.new()
assert_eq(packer.open(mod_file, ZIPPacker.APPEND_ADDINZIP), OK)
assert_eq(packer.start_file(file_name), OK)
assert_eq(packer.write_file(schema_text.to_ascii_buffer()), OK)
assert_eq(packer.close_file(), OK)
	
var script_cache := 'list=Array[Dictionary]([{
"base": &"Resource",
"class": &"%s",
"icon": "",
"language": &"GDScript",
"path": "res://%s"
}])
'%[gdscript_class_name, file_name]
assert_eq(packer.start_file(".godot/global_script_cache.cfg"), OK)
assert_eq(packer.write_file(script_cache.to_ascii_buffer()), OK)
assert_eq(packer.close_file(), OK)
assert_eq(packer.close(), OK)
	
assert_true(ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack(mod_file))
```

~I suspect I'm missing the `.godot/uid_cache.bin` file, but I'm not sure how to produce it currently.~

It works, see the solution below.

OK, so the UID cache is not needed, the above code works, I just mistyped the filename. It should be `.godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg` instead of `.godot/global_script_cache.cfg`. This is a good workaround for tests as the class name works.

What's preventing the use of an empty filepath? Is it actually used meaningfully anywhere, or just stored for the sake of it? It wouldn't be ideal, of course, but I think it would make sense for scripts generated through code. The same applies to resources, where resource_path is empty when the resource is instantiated through code.
